chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ulwan narrated from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, this fire of yours is but one-seventieth of the fire of Hell. It has been extinguished seventy times with water and then rekindled. Were that not so, no human being would have been able to bear it once it is ignited. And indeed, it will be brought on the Day of Resurrection until it is placed upon the Fire, so it will scream a scream such that no close angel nor any sent Prophet will remain but that he will go down on his knees out of dread from its scream.'
ai.seo_question: How does the intensity of earthly fire compare to the fire of Hell according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* emphasizes the qualitative superiority of Hellfire over earthly fire, a concept rooted in the Shia exegetical tradition that highlights the divine power sustaining its intensity. The narrative underscores the cosmic scale of the Day of Judgment, where the 'scream' of Hell serves as a universal sign of awe, causing even the highest angels and prophets to prostrate in reverence before God's majesty.
